name: The widow of Zarephath
charge: Making the man of God a little cake first, out of the last handful of meal, according to the word
summary: When the brook Cherith dried up, the Lord sent Elijah to Zarephath of Zidon, where He had commanded a widow to sustain him; she had only a handful of meal and a little oil, and was gathering sticks to make a last meal for herself and her son (1 Kings 17:7-12). Elijah told her to make him a little cake first, and the meal and oil did not fail until the rain came (1 Kings 17:13-16). When her son died, Elijah prayed and the child revived, and she confessed that he was a man of God and the word of the Lord in his mouth was truth (1 Kings 17:17-24). Christ named her in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:25-26).
offenseFull: The brook dried up for want of rain, and the word of the Lord sent Elijah to Zarephath, which belonged to Zidon, where He had commanded a widow woman to sustain him (1 Kings 17:7-9). The study notes stress the distance: from the east side by Jordan to the west by Sidon on the coast was a hard walk, with no water anywhere. The Jubilee class places Zarephath in Lebanon, the northern bound named when the captivity of Israel returns to possess the land of the Canaanites (Obadiah 1:20). The Lord who had commanded the ravens now commanded a widow; the class on temptation calls it a show of how mighty the prophets were, for God said, I commanded the animals, and now a woman is going to feed you.

At the gate of the city she was gathering sticks. Elijah asked her for a little water, and as she went he asked for a morsel of bread. She answered, by the Lord his God, that she had no cake, only a handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruse, and she was gathering two sticks to dress it for herself and her son, that they might eat it and die (1 Kings 17:10-12). Elijah told her not to fear, but to go and do as she had said, only to make him a little cake first and bring it to him, and afterward make for herself and her son; for the Lord God of Israel said the meal and the oil would not run out until the day He sent rain (1 Kings 17:13-14). She went and did according to the saying of Elijah (1 Kings 17:15).

The study notes draw a precept from the order: feed the man of God first; the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when He tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding; the wife is to see that she reverences her husband (Ephesians 5:33), and that reverence goes into the honour of feeding the man first, as the widow did. She was asked to give out of her last handful before she saw any increase, and for trusting the Lord and obeying she was sustained.
judgmentFull: She and Elijah and her house ate many days, and the meal and the oil did not run out, according to the word the Lord spoke by Elijah (1 Kings 17:15-16). The little she had did not run out until God sent rain on the earth again; that is the power God gave His prophets to do what is not natural.

After these things her son fell sick, so severe that there was no breath left in him. She asked Elijah whether he had come to bring her sin to mind and kill her son; her thought was that the child was paying for the parent’s sins (1 Kings 17:17-18). Elijah took the child up to the loft where he lodged, laid him on his own bed, stretched himself on him three times, and cried to the Lord to let the child’s soul come into him again. The Lord heard the voice of Elijah, the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived, and Elijah brought him down and gave him to his mother (1 Kings 17:19-23). The notes give praise that Elijah was there to call on the Lord, for it was not the young man’s time to go. A man’s days are determined, his months are numbered with the Most High, and he cannot pass the limit set for him; because the child’s day had not come, the Lord let his soul return (Job 14:1-5). She said that now she knew he was a man of God and that the word of the Lord in his mouth was truth (1 Kings 17:24).

Christ brought her up in the synagogue at Nazareth. There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut three years and six months, but Elias was sent to none of them except a widow of Sarepta, a city of Sidon; and none of the many lepers of Israel was cleansed in Elisha’s time but Naaman the Syrian. At this the synagogue was filled with wrath and tried to cast him headlong from the hill (Luke 4:25-29). Giving the Sense reads Christ’s point this way: he was not sent to everybody, just as Elijah was sent to one widow.

text.text: And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.
For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth.
And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?
And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
And he cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.
